speaker: (check key)
current_text: Sable, Tilly and Pip, dearie, all on the square. And buy a card from Sable. You are not leaving this town with only what a cave gave you.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: Back already. Sable charmed you, Tilly was a colour, and Pip measured your head without asking. Good. That is Crosspath.
new_text: Back already. Sable charmed you, Tilly was a colour, Pip measured you. That is {town}, dearie. Try leaving with the same hat.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: Here: a trophy. Everyone gets one. Don't make that face. I didn't make the rule. I did make the trophy.
new_text: Here: a trophy. Everybody gets one. I made it myself, so participate carefully.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: Now that deck of yours. A deck you never chose is a deck you will lose with.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: The Deck Station is down Champions' Road, south of the square. Swap what you like, save it to a slot, then come and tell me.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: The Deck Station, dearie. Champions' Road, south of the square. Save it to a slot, or it doesn't count. I check.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: Sorted and saved. You are starting to look like someone who means it. Starting.
new_text: Sorted and saved. Your own deck, at last. Now you may take personal offence when it loses.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: Now, a favour. Tilly's store room, the corner house beside her shop, has been moaning for a week. Not Tilly. The room.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: Ghosts, I expect. Petty ones: the worst kind. Nobody can get in for so much as a candle. Go and sort them out. Gently, if they let you.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: The store room door, beside Tilly's shop on the north side of the square. Ignore the rattling. That is just them being dramatic.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: A refund. Ninety years of haunting, over a refund. I have had customers like that. I still have one.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: Well done, dearie. You fight better than you look, and you look half drowned.
new_text: Well done, dearie. You settled the ghosts. Next, settle yourself somewhere dry.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: Right. Time you had something sharper than a deck. Bertram Beetsworth issues gear, at the smithy on the west side of the square.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: He is... thorough. Report to him, do what he asks, and do not touch his drawer.

speaker: (check key)
current_text: Bertram's smithy, west side of the square. Win him a fight, any fight, and he will stamp something. He lives to stamp something.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: There is a door under the old well that has been locked since before I was born.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: I always thought the key was lost. It was not, dearie. Somebody hid it in a chest in this very town. Find it, and we will see what the door is for.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: The key is in a hidden chest somewhere in town. Look in the odd corners. This town has a great many odd corners. I am one of them.
new_text: The key is in a hidden chest in town. Look in the odd corners, dearie. This town has never quite managed a straight one.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: You found it. Look at the bow: four little carvings, in a ring. Hm. Never mind. I am too old for stairs, dearie. You are not.

speaker: Elder Maren
current_text: The iron hatch beside the well. Go on. Whatever is under it belonged to the Old Kingdom, not to me. Mind the stairs.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
current_text: Only the worthy reach the top. Also bring water.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
current_text: There's a mountain behind the station... and a barbell on top older than the regime. Older than me, nearly. Bring me a protein shake from the stand and I'll show you the way. Can't climb on an empty cup.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
current_text: Water, friend. A protein shake from the stand will do. Don't spill it. I spilled one, the Festival year... where was I.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
current_text: That's the best water I've ever seen. Thank you. Rule one: never lift alone. Rule two... rule two was water.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
current_text: The way up Mount Swolympus is open. The trail behind the station. Mind the thin air... it's very... thin.
new_text: Mount Swolympus is open. Take the trail behind the station. Mind the thin air... never gets enough credit for being there.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Basil
current_text: Over here. Quietly. Have you ever eaten somewhere with no menu? ...I'm brave. I'm brave.

speaker: Basil
current_text: There's a golden reservation card hidden in one of the Buffet's stashes: 'Seating: 1. Courses: 3. Survival: optional.' Find it and I'll tell you where to sit.

speaker: Basil
current_text: The card is in one of the hidden stashes around the Buffet. Golden. You'll know it. Chef always said gold means sit down.

speaker: Basil
current_text: That's the card! One seat, three courses, survival optional. Oh, I'm so excited I could whisk.
new_text: That's it! One seat, three courses, survival optional. I'm excited. I think. It feels a lot like the other thing.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Basil
current_text: The sliding door to Omakase is open. Leave your fate to the chef. (quietly) Yes, Chef.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
current_text: Number 4,000,212? That's me. They're on 3. Can you help?

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
current_text: The queue in the Waiting Room of Eternity is stuck. Process two of the roaming staff on the D.N.A. floors and I'll get you in. I've brought a book. Several.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
current_text: Two roaming staff on the D.N.A. floors. The queue will not move on its own. I've checked. For some decades.
new_text: Process two roaming staff on the D.N.A. floors. The queue will not move itself. I've given it a very fair chance.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
current_text: Two fewer. The queue moved! Slightly. I felt it in my ticket.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
current_text: The Waiting Room of Eternity will see you now. Take a number. Not mine, please. I've grown attached.
new_text: The Waiting Room of Eternity will see you now. Take a number. Please leave mine; we've been through so much together.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: SOMEBODY has been eating ALL the compost. Little paw prints. A tiny crown.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: Chase off two of the scavengers in the Dump and the trail will lead you to the alley under the big dumpster. Gently, please. They're only hungry. And GUILTY.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: Two scavengers. The paw prints are fresh. So is the smell of stolen compost.
new_text: Two scavengers in the Dump. Fresh paw prints, freshly stolen compost. A trail of evidence with TERRIBLE table manners.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: The paw prints lead to the big dumpster. I knew it. I KNEW it.

speaker: Brother Bramble
current_text: Under the tipped-over dumpster there's a gate made from a bicycle wheel. That's the way to the Trash Panda Throne. Bring a peg for your nose.

speaker: Kestrel
current_text: Psst. Down. The enforcers walk this road on the hour, and they hate surprises. I'm a surprise.

speaker: Kestrel
current_text: Kestrel. I scout for the Wrinkles. Going into the city? There's an older way in than the gate. Follow the chalk, not the guards. The guards are worse at drawing.

speaker: Kestrel
current_text: Road's clear. For now. Give it ten minutes and it won't be. Chalk's still fresh.
new_text: Road's clear for ten minutes. Chalk's fresh. Move while the guards are busy being punctual somewhere else.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Kestrel
current_text: There's an older way into the city. Nobody remembers it. That's the point.

speaker: Kestrel
current_text: Get yourself inside and find Wren in the Crease. She'll tell you what the old tunnels are for. Then I'll show you the hatch. Deal?

speaker: Kestrel
current_text: Get inside and find the Crease: the manhole near the gate. Knock three times. Not two. Two is rude. Then ask Wren about the tunnels.

speaker: Kestrel
current_text: You found them. Told you I'd be here. Didn't say where. That's the fun part. Here, you've earned this.

speaker: Kestrel
current_text: The hatch in the north-east of the Outskirts, under the wall, goes down to the Old Service Tunnels. Mind the patrols. And mind my chalk.

speaker: Kestrel
current_text: The grate beneath the plaza lifts with a groan. Light from the perfect city pours in, and behind you the old tunnels run on: four Paths' services, still connected.

speaker: Kestrel
current_text: You climb up past the walls. Nobody is watching this way in. Nobody remembers it. That is the point.

speaker: Baron Quadzilla, the Leg Press Lord
current_text: On a throne that is really a leg press, a Beefcake with thighs like mill wheels pushes a sled of plates up and down, up and down. He has not stood up in years.

speaker: Baron Quadzilla, the Leg Press Lord
current_text: 'Nobody. Skips. Leg day,' he says, between reps. 'In my cave. Show me yours.'
new_text: 'Nobody. Skips. Leg day.' He presses another rep. 'In my cave. Show me yours. No standing ovation required.'
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Baron Quadzilla, the Leg Press Lord
current_text: Baron Quadzilla racks the plates, stands, and wobbles. 'Huh,' he says. 'Standing. Wobbly. Like a first rep.'

speaker: Baron Quadzilla, the Leg Press Lord
current_text: He hands you a sweaty ribbon. 'Leg day survivor. Wear it with pride. And stretch.'
new_text: He hands you a sweaty ribbon. 'Leg day survivor. Wear it. Stretch. That order.'
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: The Ancient Spotter
current_text: A stone colossus sits at the summit with its hands out, palms up, waiting for a barbell. It has been spotting for a thousand years. It is very, very ready.

speaker: The Ancient Spotter
current_text: 'Lift,' it rumbles. 'I will catch it. I have always caught it.'

speaker: The Ancient Spotter
current_text: The Ancient Spotter lowers its hands and, for the first time in a thousand years, sets something down. The barbell on the altar is yours.

speaker: The Ancient Spotter
current_text: 'One more rep,' it says. Then, quieter: '...That was the one. Thank you for coming up.'

speaker: The Itamae Supreme
current_text: The Itamae Supreme lifts a long knife and does not look up. 'Omakase.'

speaker: The Itamae Supreme
current_text: Behind him, a bull made of toro lowers its horns, politely.

speaker: The Itamae Supreme
current_text: The Itamae bows, wipes his knife on a cloth and slides a small plate across the counter. 'Omakase,' he says. This time it sounds like thank you.

speaker: Betty Bones, Surly Secretary
current_text: A single desk under a single green lamp, buried in forms. Betty Bones looks up through cat-eye glasses, very slowly, and sighs the sigh of the long deceased.

speaker: Betty Bones, Surly Secretary
current_text: 'Forms A through F,' she says. 'Then we'll talk. We won't, but still.'

speaker: Betty Bones, Surly Secretary
current_text: Betty stamps one last form with a bony flourish. 'Fine. Number 4,000,212 is approved. Don't make it a thing.'

speaker: Betty Bones, Surly Secretary
current_text: Far down the line, a ghost with a crumpled ticket begins, very quietly, to cheer.

speaker: His Majesty the Raccoon
current_text: The Throne of Lids creaks. On it sits a very large raccoon in a very small crown, sweating profusely.

speaker: His Majesty the Raccoon
current_text: 'WE DID NOT EAT THE COMPOST,' says His Majesty. 'We... sampled it. We would be glad to explain, after you leave.'
new_text: 'WE DID NOT EAT THE COMPOST. We sampled it.' His Majesty grips the throne. 'The royal tasting is not open to questions.'
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: His Majesty the Raccoon
current_text: His Majesty abdicates with great dignity and a crust of pizza. The crown rolls under the throne.

speaker: His Majesty the Raccoon
current_text: 'The compost was for the kingdom,' he says. 'We are the kingdom. Checkmate.'
new_text: 'Compost is for the kingdom,' he says. 'We are the kingdom. We fail to see the problem. Do not point at the crumbs.'
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Captain Spotless
current_text: A grate lets in light from a perfect city. Beneath it stands Captain Spotless, polishing his shield with a sleeve he has already polished.

speaker: Captain Spotless
current_text: 'HALT. These tunnels do not exist. You are standing in nothing. I cannot allow you to have found it.'

speaker: Captain Spotless
current_text: The Captain sits down on a barrel and, for a moment, looks very tired. 'I remember when these tunnels were full of people,' he says.

speaker: Captain Spotless
current_text: 'All four Paths, shoulder to shoulder, and nobody measuring anybody. Go on. The grate is not locked.'

speaker: The Vault Guardian, the Old Kingdom Automaton
current_text: A four-coloured core hums at the heart of the vault, four marks set in a ring. Beside it a clockwork guardian unfolds, with a sound like a very old clock remembering the hour.

speaker: The Vault Guardian, the Old Kingdom Automaton
current_text: 'Tick. Identify,' it says. 'The Old Kingdom's banner is not for just anyone.'

speaker: The Vault Guardian, the Old Kingdom Automaton
current_text: The Automaton clicks, whirs and lowers one knee. In its outstretched hand, folded neatly, is the Old Kingdom's banner.

speaker: The Vault Guardian, the Old Kingdom Automaton
current_text: 'Tick. ...Recognised. Four Paths. One kingdom. Carry it well.'

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The hatch opens on white light and a smell of disinfectant. A staircase of clean steel goes down through the roots of the forest where you woke up.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Everything about this place is familiar in the way a bruise is familiar. You do not know why your hands are shaking. You go down anyway.

speaker: Dr. Ambrose Siphon, Chief Path-ologist
current_text: A round chamber, glass on every side, a chair at the center with straps worn pale. Cables run from the chair to four great tanks, each glowing a different color. This is where it was done.

speaker: Dr. Ambrose Siphon, Chief Path-ologist
current_text: The tanks are still half full: four colors of a boy's power, bottled, labelled and filed. A Path-ologist in a stained coat says, without looking up, 'Subject 1 is not to leave the chair.'

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Drain Warden falls across the chair. The cables go slack, and the four tanks flicker, as if something in them has noticed you.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The power is not yours to take back this way. It was never meant to be bottled at all.

speaker: The Rescuer
current_text: In a cell at the end of the corridor, a figure in a torn gray travelling cloak sits with their hands bound. They do not look up. The hood is a rag; the pin at the throat is bent.

speaker: The Rescuer
current_text: 'You came back,' they say. 'I told them you would not. I told them nobody could be that stubborn.'
new_text: 'You came back,' they say. 'I hoped you would. I told them you would not.'
writer_note: Lab reunion: keeps protective lie and warmth without a stubbornness punchline.

speaker: The Rescuer
current_text: The lock gives way. The Rescuer pushes the hood down at last, and the face under it is tired and kind and unmistakable: the person who knelt beside you in the forest.

speaker: The Rescuer
current_text: 'I never told you my name,' they say. 'I will, once you have taken this place apart. Go on. I will walk behind you.'

speaker: Dr. Ambrose Siphon, Chief Path-ologist
current_text: Dr. Ambrose Siphon, Chief Path-ologist, looks up from a bench of humming glass. Neat, polite, delighted, and not at all surprised.

speaker: Dr. Ambrose Siphon, Chief Path-ologist
current_text: 'Subject 1! You came back to us. And you've grown. Remarkable. The draining has been very good for your posture.'
new_text: 'Subject 1. You came back to us. You have grown. Remarkable, after so many cycles. I must examine the records.'
writer_note: Clinical horror, without a joke about the effect of captivity on his body.

speaker: Dr. Ambrose Siphon, Chief Path-ologist
current_text: '{villain}'s rule was always a bit crude. I never needed a crown, only the research. My assistant left us too, you know. Confused, poor thing. Assistants come home.'

speaker: Dr. Ambrose Siphon, Chief Path-ologist
current_text: 'Please, sit. This will only drain a little.'

speaker: Dr. Ambrose Siphon, Chief Path-ologist
current_text: Siphon's equipment goes dark, tank by tank. He sags against a bench, and for once he does not look fascinated.

speaker: Dr. Ambrose Siphon, Chief Path-ologist
current_text: 'You are not a Subject,' he says, dazed. 'You were never a Subject. Maren said so, and I called it sentimentality.'

speaker: Dr. Ambrose Siphon, Chief Path-ologist
current_text: The tanks go clear. The four colors rise out of them, through the roof and into the forest, where the trees lean toward them like flowers. You do not feel stronger. You feel less alone.

speaker: Dr. Ambrose Siphon, Chief Path-ologist
